newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish finmin says GNP to grow at 5.5 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Irish finmin says GNP to grow at 5.5 pct in 1997.

text.p: Ireland's gross national product (GNP) will grow by around 5.5 percent in 1997 and should average 4.5 percent in 1998 and 1999, Irish Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn said in his budget speech on Wednesday.
This follows GNP growth of over seven percent in 1995 and estimates of GNP growth of around six percent in 1996.
Quinn said inflation is expected to be moderate at just over two percent per year in the three-year period from 1997 to 1999.
The annual average rise in the CPI in 1996 was 1.6 percent.
He said employment growth should average about 38,000 per year over the period.
Employment increased by around 50,000 in 1996 on top of a rise of 45,000 the year before.

Quinn said his three-year programme was aimed at offering up tax reductions of one billion pounds per annum on a full-year cost basis and an action programme for social inclusion and equality involving expenditure of 525 million pounds.
"A major start has been made today in implementing these "Partnership 2000" commitments in this 1997 budget," he said.
He said his growth, inflation and employment forecasts were working assumptions for his programme.
